Al Falah University founder Jawad Ahmed Siddiqui at the Enforcement Directorate headquarters in a PMLA case amid the Red Fort blast probe, in New Delhi, Monday, Dec. 1, 2025. File | Photo Credit: PTI
The Delhi High Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) granted seven-day custody parole to Al Falah University group chairman Jawad Ahmed Siddiqui, who is in custody in two money laundering cases, to take care of his ailing wife.
The court passed the order after hearing Siddiqui’s plea seeking interim bail or custody parole for a week on medical and humanitarian grounds.
Mr Siddiqui said his wife is a Stage-4 ovarian cancer patient and has to undergo the next cycle of chemotherapy on November 10.
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) opposed Siddiqui’s interim release as the allegations against him were serious. The ED’s counsel submitted that the accused was a flight risk and had criminal antecedents, including his involvement in the November 2025 Red Fort car blast case.
In July, the high court had refused to grant interim bail to Siddiqui and permitted him to meet his wife on custody parole on three dates.
One case is linked to the alleged generation of illicit funds from the fees paid by students of the university. He was arrested on November 18, 2025, in the case registered under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).
The ED’s probe stems from two FIRs by the Delhi Police Crime Branch alleging that Al Falah University falsely projected NAAC accreditation and UGC recognition to mislead students and parents.
Al Falah University came under scrutiny in a ‘white-collar terror’ probe in which two doctors linked to it were arrested, while another, Umar-un-Nabi, was identified as the suicide bomber in the November 10, 2025, blast outside the Red Fort that killed 15 people.
